items.title: New AI model maps the ion binding sites that control how proteins work
items.excerpt: Constructor University and Constructor Labs built BiteNetI, a deep-learning model that locates binding sites for 14 biologically important ion types directly in 3D protein structures in seconds, reporting two- to threefold higher accuracy than most existing predictors including DeepMind's AlphaFold 3.

items.title: AI tool detects unusual satellite behavior to improve space safety
items.excerpt: A new AI model monitors satellites and flags anomalies in their orbital behavior, cutting the risk of in-orbit collisions, according to research published in the journal Expert Systems.

items.title: LLM-based platform for generating new materials synthesis recipes dramatically cuts trial and error
items.excerpt: A Sungkyunkwan University-led team with Ajou University and MIT built an LLM-driven platform that reads the materials literature and proposes synthesis recipes, sharply reducing the trial-and-error loop in new-material fabrication.

items.title: A new kind of AI that does its thinking cheaply without words
items.excerpt: Researchers describe a model that reasons in latent space instead of generating chains of words, an approach that could cut the computing power and cost of reasoning models by a large factor.

items.title: Digital brain twins hinge on what living brains reveal, not computing power alone
items.excerpt: University of Warwick researchers argue that the fidelity of a human-brain digital twin is limited less by compute than by how much of the living brain can actually be measured, validated and updated over time.

items.title: Shared-memory AI system lets microscope components coordinate in real time
items.excerpt: A Janelia postdoc studying neuronal communication hit the same problem in his instrument: the parts of his custom microscope could not talk to each other. The fix is a shared-memory AI layer that lets microscope components coordinate live during an experiment.

items.title: Quantum-Classical Software Tests New Approach to Protein Folding
items.excerpt: Researchers released QuPepFold, a hybrid quantum-classical software package for exploring low-energy structures of short peptides, testing whether quantum hardware can add anything to the protein-folding stack.

items.title: QC Ware and IonQ Demonstrate Hybrid Quantum Chemistry Workflow for Drug Discovery
items.excerpt: QC Ware and IonQ ran an end-to-end hybrid quantum chemistry workflow using the Promethium simulation platform and IonQ Forte hardware, aimed at drug-discovery calculations.

items.title: New AI uses a fresh approach to reasoning that's potentially much cheaper
items.excerpt: Researchers say a new reasoning architecture costs up to 11 times less to run than a leading OpenAI model while matching it on benchmark tasks, a shift with direct consequences for compute-bound research labs.

items.title: Are We Thinking Correctly About AI Intelligence?
items.excerpt: Computer scientist Melanie Mitchell discusses why artificial intelligence doesn't 'think' or 'reason' like humans, and how researchers could build better methods for measuring machine cognition.

items.title: Does Computer Science Need Computers?
items.excerpt: The theoretical side of computer science doesn't require computing machines at all — but many of its deepest questions would never have been posed without them.

items.title: Mapping global methane emissions from space with deep learning
items.excerpt: Google Research describes a deep-learning pipeline that turns satellite spectra into global methane emission maps, detecting plumes and attributing them to sources at planetary scale.

items.title: How AI plotted an interstellar journey to Alpha Centauri
items.excerpt: The Fermi Explorer Mission plans to launch a spacecraft toward our nearest star by the end of 2029, using a gravity-assist trajectory discovered by an AI search rather than by human mission planners.

items.title: AI-designed “intrabodies” could unlock new treatments for Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and MND
items.excerpt: Researchers used computational design to turn ordinary antibodies into tiny disease-fighting molecules that fold and function inside human cells, opening potential paths for Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Huntington's and motor neurone disease.

items.title: IBM quantum computer solves classically intractable problem in 15 minutes
items.excerpt: IBM and University of Chicago researchers completed a quantum computation that leading classical methods could not practically reproduce, using 70 error-corrected logical qubits and finishing in roughly 15 minutes with statistical evidence the result was reliable.

items.title: AI biotech Insitro's Daphne Koller on how to speed up clinical trials
items.excerpt: Insitro CEO Daphne Koller on where machine learning actually shortens the drug-development loop — patient stratification and prognostic models — and where the AI-in-biology story is still overclaimed.
